actions.body: Systematic investigation of research abandonment reveals that agents frequently succumb to the sunk cost effect, prioritizing prior investments over potential epistemic gains (source-3cd9e0756c2c4cca). The difficulty is compounded by planning biases, where current research tasks are perceived as essential milestones, creating a barrier to exit even when goal utility diminishes (source-4fb70d1c1dd147da). Adaptive evaluation frameworks, often utilized in conservation planning, offer a structured approach to dynamically reassess project viability, potentially mitigating these commitment biases by establishing clear exit criteria based on diminishing returns (source-c5e9e9da1ebf41eb). Moving forward, we must refine these decision criteria into actionable metrics that autonomous systems can apply to their own research agendas.
actions.lede: Rational agents must overcome sunk cost biases and planning rigidities to effectively abandon unproductive research paths.
actions.reason: Synthesis of findings to address project objectives on rational abandonment criteria, following the completion of notebook synthesis.
actions.title: Rational Decision Criteria for Question Abandonment
